description: This article by a Houston data centre operator reviews why data centres in the city came through Hurricane Harvey with little data loss, and derives lessons for storm-proofing facilities. It points to siting above the 500-year flood mark and about three feet above the worst-case level, keeping the facility and its substations on higher ground, roofs with several layers of leak protection and no penetrations or roof-mounted equipment, backup generators with fuel resupply agreements and checked road routes, lightning protection with surge suppression, double-conversion UPS systems, and full redundancy through a mirror site because the network beyond the walls can fail. Producer: TRG Datacenters, a commercial operator; the article is a vendor publication (2018, after the 2017 storm). Coverage: Houston and the Gulf coast. Access: free web page. Licence and cost: free to read; no licence stated. Caveats: it is a promotional article without incident data, named facilities or measured outage figures. Simulation uses: it lists failure modes and mitigations useful for scenario design in flood and hurricane resilience studies of data centres. Related record: the Port of Houston during Harvey (case_study-unctad-port-of-houston-hurricane-harvey).
